Estimate abundance and density from removal samples

Source: R/abundance.R
abundance.Rd

Abundance is estimated as \(\hat N = T / P\), where \(T\) is the total catch over the passes of a sample and \(P\) is the cumulative capture probability, see capture_prob.

Usage

abundance(
  object,
  newdata = NULL,
  area = NULL,
  by = NULL,
  target = c("realised", "expected"),
  level = 0.95
)

Arguments

object

an efp2 fitted model

newdata

an optional data.frame as for capture_prob, which must also contain the counts used as the response in the model

area

an optional name of a column in the data giving the area fished, or a vector of areas with one value per row of the data. If given, density (abundance per unit area) is also returned. With by, the area must be the same for all samples in a group.

by

an optional character vector of the names of variables in the data, which must be the same for all passes of a sample. Abundance is summed over the samples with each combination of their values.

target

the abundance to estimate, "realised" (the default) or "expected", see Details

level

the confidence level

Value

a data.frame with one row per sample, in the order the samples first appear in the data, with columns id, catch the total catch, P, N the estimated abundance, its standard error se, and confidence limits lower and upper. If area is given there are also columns area, density, density_lower and density_upper. With by there is one row per group, sorted by the by variables, with the by variables and nsample, the number of samples, in place of id and P.

Details

Two targets are available, which have the same estimate but different standard errors:

"realised"

the number of fish \(N\) present when the sample was taken. Given \(N\), the catch is binomial, \(T \sim \textrm{Bin}(N, P)\), and (Huggins, 1989) $$\textrm{var}(\hat N) \approx \hat N (1 - P) / P + \hat N^2 (1 - P)^2 \textrm{var}(\textrm{logit}(P)).$$ The lower confidence limit is not less than the catch.

"expected"

the expected number of fish \(\lambda\), for example density times area, when the number present is \(N \sim \textrm{Poisson}(\lambda)\). The catch is then \(T \sim \textrm{Poisson}(\lambda P)\), and the first term of the variance is \(\hat\lambda / P\), which also includes the natural variation of \(N\) about \(\lambda\). The standard error is larger by a factor of about \(1 / \sqrt{1 - P}\) when \(P\) is well estimated.

Use "realised" to say how many fish were present, and "expected" to describe the underlying abundance, for example when comparing sites or years. A Poisson model for the counts with offset \(\log(A P)\), where \(A\) is the area, is a model for the expected abundance.

Confidence intervals are computed on the log scale. When the total catch is zero the estimated abundance is zero and the confidence limits are NA.

With by, abundance is summed over the samples in each group, for example over the lifestages caught at a site in a year. The variation in the catches is independent between samples, but the estimates of \(P\) are correlated, as they depend on the same model coefficients, and this is allowed for: $$\textrm{var}(\sum_s \hat N_s) \approx \sum_s v_s + w^\top \Sigma w,$$ where \(v_s\) is \(\hat N_s (1 - P_s) / P_s\) for the realised abundance and \(\hat N_s / P_s\) for the expected abundance, \(w_s = \hat N_s (1 - P_s)\) and \(\Sigma\) is the covariance matrix of \(\textrm{logit}(P_s)\).

References

Huggins, R. M. (1989) On the statistical analysis of capture experiments. Biometrika, 76, 133-140. doi:10.1093/biomet/76.1.133

See also

capture_prob

Examples

ef2_data$pass12 <- factor(pmin(ef2_data$pass, 2))
ef2_data$sampleID <- as.numeric(factor(paste(ef2_data$date,
  ef2_data$siteID, ef2_data$lifestage)))
ef2_data <- ef2_data[order(ef2_data$sampleID, ef2_data$pass), ]
m1 <- efp2(count ~ lifestage + pass12, data = ef2_data,
  pass = pass, id = sampleID)
head(abundance(m1, area = "area"))
#>   id catch         P          N        se lower      upper area    density
#> 1  1    49 0.9460482  51.794403 1.8495074    49  55.549234  122 0.42454429
#> 2  2    42 0.9858539  42.602661 0.7975209    42  44.194802  122 0.34920214
#> 3  3    10 0.9460482  10.570286 0.7888318    10  12.235159  227 0.04656514
#> 4  4   132 0.9858539 133.894076 1.4715777   132 136.809604  227 0.58984174
#> 5  5     5 0.9460482   5.285143 0.5534132     5   6.489138  228 0.02318045
#> 6  6    64 0.9858539  64.918340 0.9944564    64  66.896993  228 0.28472956
#>   density_lower density_upper
#> 1    0.40163934    0.45532159
#> 2    0.34426230    0.36225248
#> 3    0.04405286    0.05389938
#> 4    0.58149780    0.60268548
#> 5    0.02192982    0.02846113
#> 6    0.28070175    0.29340787

# summed over lifestages for each site and year
head(abundance(m1, area = "area", by = c("siteID", "year")))
#>   siteID year nsample catch         N       se    lower     upper area

# expected abundance, for comparing years
abundance(m1, by = "year", target = "expected")
